verses.1: Do not make for yourselves idols, or set up carved images or pillars, or place sacred stones in your land to bow down to them, for I am the LORD your God.
verses.2: Keep my Sabbaths and reverence my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
verses.3: If you walk in my statutes and keep my commandments and do them,
verses.4: I will give you timely rain, and the land will yield its produce, and the trees of the field will bear their fruit.
verses.5: Your threshing will reach into the harvest, and your harvest will reach into the time of planting, and you will eat your bread to your satisfaction and live securely in your land.
verses.6: I will grant peace in the land, and you will sleep untroubled, with no one to scare you. I will remove dangerous beasts from the land, and no sword will pass through your land.
verses.7: You will chase your enemies, and they will fall before you by the sword.
verses.8: Five of you will chase a hundred, and a hundred will chase ten thousand. Your enemies will fall before you by the sword.
verses.9: I will look upon you with favor and multiply you, and I will confirm my covenant with you.
verses.10: You will eat the old harvest, and you will clear out the old to make way for the new.
verses.11: I will place my covenant in you and will not despise you.
verses.12: I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be my people.
verses.13: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, where you were slaves, and who broke the yoke of your burden and led you to walk uprightly.
verses.14: But if you do not obey me and do not carry out all these commandments,
verses.15: if you reject my statutes, and if your hearts despise my judgments so that you do not carry out all my commandments, breaking my covenant,
verses.16: I will do this to you: I will bring upon you panic, consumption, and a fever that melts the eyes and consumes the soul. You will sow your seed in vain, for your enemies will eat it.
verses.17: I will turn my face against you, and you will be struck down before your enemies. Those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee though no one is pursuing you.
verses.18: If even then you do not listen to me, I will discipline you seven times over for your sins.
verses.19: I will break the pride of your strength and make the sky over you like iron and the ground under you like bronze.
verses.20: Your strength will be spent in vain, and the land will not yield its produce, and the trees of the land will not bear their fruit.
verses.21: And if you walk contrary to me and do not want to listen to me, I will bring upon you plagues seven times over for your sins.
verses.22: I will let wild animals come into your land and destroy you and your livestock, reduce your numbers, and make your roads desolate.
verses.23: If you still do not take discipline but walk contrary to me,
verses.24: I will walk among you in wrath, and I will strike you seven times over for your sins.
verses.25: I will bring a sword of judgment upon you, and you will flee into your cities. I will send plague among you, and you will be given over to your enemies.
verses.26: When I reduce your food supply, ten women will bake your bread in a single oven, and they will give your bread by measure, and you will eat but not be satisfied.
verses.27: If even then you do not listen to me, but walk contrary to me,
verses.28: I will walk among you in fury, and I will discipline you seven times over for your sins.
verses.29: You will eat the flesh of your sons and the flesh of your daughters.
verses.30: I will destroy your altars and cut down your sacred pillars, and I will cast your carcases on the carcases of your idols, and my soul will despise you.
verses.31: I will make your cities a wasteland, and I will lay waste your sanctuaries, and I will take no delight in the fragrance of your offerings.
verses.32: I will make the land desolate, and your enemies who dwell in it will be appalled.
verses.33: I will scatter you among the nations, and the sword will consume you. Your land will become desolate, and your cities will become wastelands.
verses.34: Then the land will enjoy its sabbaths for all the years of its desolation, while you are in the land of your enemies. Then the land will rest and enjoy its sabbaths.
verses.35: For all the years it did not rest during your sabbaths, when you dwelled upon it.
verses.36: Those who remain among you I will cause to grow faint-hearted in the land of their enemies. A leaf’s whisper will chase them, and they will flee as one flees from war, though no one will pursue them.
verses.37: Each brother will fall before his brother, as if pursued by the sword, with no one to rescue you from your enemies.
verses.38: You will be destroyed among the nations, and the land of your enemies will consume you.
verses.39: Those who are left among you will rot away for their sins in the land of their enemies, as well as for the sins of their ancestors.
verses.40: They will confess their sin and the sin of their ancestors, their rebellion and how they walked contrary to me.
verses.41: I will also walk contrary to them in wrath, and I will bring them into the land of their enemies—or their hearts may finally be circumcised, and then they will accept their guilt.
verses.42: I will remember my covenant with Jacob, my covenant with Isaac, and my covenant with Abraham, and I will remember the land.
verses.43: The land will be abandoned by them, and it will enjoy its sabbaths during its desolation by them. Then they will accept their guilt, for they despised my judgments and rejected my statutes.
verses.44: But even when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them or despise them so as to destroy them and break my covenant with them, for I am the LORD their God.
verses.45: I will remember the covenant I made with them when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, before the nations, to be their God. I am the LORD.
verses.46: These are the statutes, judgments, and teachings that the LORD gave to Israel on Mount Sinai through Moses.

notes:
Notes
- v. 29: "You will eat the flesh of your sons and the flesh of your daughters" — a literal translation of the Hebrew, reflecting a severe curse.
- v. 41: "their hearts may finally be circumcised" — a reference to spiritual transformation, using "circumcised" as a metaphor for inner change.
- v. 42: "I will remember the covenant I made with them" — "remember" here implies fulfilling or acting in accordance with the covenant.
- v. 45: "before the nations" — the Hebrew is clear that this refers to the nations witnessing the covenant.
raw:
[1] Do not make for yourselves idols, or set up carved images or pillars, or place sacred stones in your land to bow down to them, for I am the LORD your God.

[2] Keep my Sabbaths and reverence my sanctuary. I am the LORD.

[3] If you walk in my statutes and keep my commandments and do them,

[4] I will give you timely rain, and the land will yield its produce, and the trees of the field will bear their fruit.

[5] Your threshing will reach into the harvest, and your harvest will reach into the time of planting, and you will eat your bread to your satisfaction and live securely in your land.

[6] I will grant peace in the land, and you will sleep untroubled, with no one to scare you. I will remove dangerous beasts from the land, and no sword will pass through your land.

[7] You will chase your enemies, and they will fall before you by the sword.

[8] Five of you will chase a hundred, and a hundred will chase ten thousand. Your enemies will fall before you by the sword.

[9] I will look upon you with favor and multiply you, and I will confirm my covenant with you.

[10] You will eat the old harvest, and you will clear out the old to make way for the new.

[11] I will place my covenant in you and will not despise you.

[12] I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be my people.

[13] I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, where you were slaves, and who broke the yoke of your burden and led you to walk uprightly.

[14] But if you do not obey me and do not carry out all these commandments,

[15] if you reject my statutes, and if your hearts despise my judgments so that you do not carry out all my commandments, breaking my covenant,

[16] I will do this to you: I will bring upon you panic, consumption, and a fever that melts the eyes and consumes the soul. You will sow your seed in vain, for your enemies will eat it.

[17] I will turn my face against you, and you will be struck down before your enemies. Those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee though no one is pursuing you.

[18] If even then you do not listen to me, I will discipline you seven times over for your sins.

[19] I will break the pride of your strength and make the sky over you like iron and the ground under you like bronze.

[20] Your strength will be spent in vain, and the land will not yield its produce, and the trees of the land will not bear their fruit.

[21] And if you walk contrary to me and do not want to listen to me, I will bring upon you plagues seven times over for your sins.

[22] I will let wild animals come into your land and destroy you and your livestock, reduce your numbers, and make your roads desolate.

[23] If you still do not take discipline but walk contrary to me,

[24] I will walk among you in wrath, and I will strike you seven times over for your sins.

[25] I will bring a sword of judgment upon you, and you will flee into your cities. I will send plague among you, and you will be given over to your enemies.

[26] When I reduce your food supply, ten women will bake your bread in a single oven, and they will give your bread by measure, and you will eat but not be satisfied.

[27] If even then you do not listen to me, but walk contrary to me,

[28] I will walk among you in fury, and I will discipline you seven times over for your sins.

[29] You will eat the flesh of your sons and the flesh of your daughters.

[30] I will destroy your altars and cut down your sacred pillars, and I will cast your carcases on the carcases of your idols, and my soul will despise you.

[31] I will make your cities a wasteland, and I will lay waste your sanctuaries, and I will take no delight in the fragrance of your offerings.

[32] I will make the land desolate, and your enemies who dwell in it will be appalled.

[33] I will scatter you among the nations, and the sword will consume you. Your land will become desolate, and your cities will become wastelands.

[34] Then the land will enjoy its sabbaths for all the years of its desolation, while you are in the land of your enemies. Then the land will rest and enjoy its sabbaths.

[35] For all the years it did not rest during your sabbaths, when you dwelled upon it.

[36] Those who remain among you I will cause to grow faint-hearted in the land of their enemies. A leaf’s whisper will chase them, and they will flee as one flees from war, though no one will pursue them.

[37] Each brother will fall before his brother, as if pursued by the sword, with no one to rescue you from your enemies.

[38] You will be destroyed among the nations, and the land of your enemies will consume you.

[39] Those who are left among you will rot away for their sins in the land of their enemies, as well as for the sins of their ancestors.

[40] They will confess their sin and the sin of their ancestors, their rebellion and how they walked contrary to me.

[41] I will also walk contrary to them in wrath, and I will bring them into the land of their enemies—or their hearts may finally be circumcised, and then they will accept their guilt.

[42] I will remember my covenant with Jacob, my covenant with Isaac, and my covenant with Abraham, and I will remember the land.

[43] The land will be abandoned by them, and it will enjoy its sabbaths during its desolation by them. Then they will accept their guilt, for they despised my judgments and rejected my statutes.

[44] But even when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them or despise them so as to destroy them and break my covenant with them, for I am the LORD their God.

[45] I will remember the covenant I made with them when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, before the nations, to be their God. I am the LORD.

[46] These are the statutes, judgments, and teachings that the LORD gave to Israel on Mount Sinai through Moses.

---
Notes
- v. 29: "You will eat the flesh of your sons and the flesh of your daughters" — a literal translation of the Hebrew, reflecting a severe curse.
- v. 41: "their hearts may finally be circumcised" — a reference to spiritual transformation, using "circumcised" as a metaphor for inner change.
- v. 42: "I will remember the covenant I made with them" — "remember" here implies fulfilling or acting in accordance with the covenant.
- v. 45: "before the nations" — the Hebrew is clear that this refers to the nations witnessing the covenant.
